note: Inputs only: partial current efficiencies at a fixed nitrate conversion (70 %), one row per potential x product.

files.extracted.csv: tidy long: one row per potential x product

csv_columns.conversion_pct: nitrate conversion at which CE was evaluated (caption)
csv_columns.species: NO2, NH3, N2 or total_excl_H2 (sum of the partial CEs, i.e. all reactions except H2 evolution)

provenance.citation: Katsounaros I., Electrochemical reduction of nitrate on tin cathode - removal of nitrate from ion-exchange resin regeneration wastes, PhD thesis (in Greek), Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Dept. of Chemical Engineering (2009)
provenance.caption_translated: Table 6.11. Partial current efficiencies of the reduction products and total current efficiency during nitrate reduction at various potentials. Electrolyte: 0.05 M NaNO3 in 2 M NaCl. Degree of conversion: 70 %. Columns: E/V | %CE NO2- | %CE NH3 | %CE N2 | %CE (total).
provenance.source_file: page text layer from the archive's online reader (scratch only, not committed)
provenance.licence: National Archive of PhD Theses terms: research use with no direct or indirect financial benefit; author must be cited; items protected by copyright

header_reconstruction: The text layer flattens the header to '% CE % CE % CE E / V % CE − NH N NO 2 3 2'. Column order NO2-, NH3, N2, total was taken from the subscript order (2, 3, 2) and confirmed by (i) the first column falling from 1.32 to 0.07 % as the text says the final nitrite concentration fell with potential, (ii) the parts summing to the printed total in every row, and (iii) the repository digitization of Diag 6.7 (data/digitized_inputs/katsounaros2009thesis_diag6p7_endpoint_vs_e), whose -2.0 V endpoint (71.6 % conversion) gives NO2-/NH3 = 0.364 and NH3/N2 = 0.398 mol/mol against 0.364 and 0.401 implied here with 2, 8 and 10 electrons.

conditions.cathode: Sn foil, 2 cm2 geometric, polished (#1200) before each run
conditions.cell: Teflon divided cell, Nafion 117 (H+), 10 mL per compartment, platinized Pt anode 6 cm2 at 2 cm, Luggin capillary
conditions.stirring: He 12 mL/min sparged at the cell bottom (also carrier to the on-line GC)
conditions.ce_definition: Appendix 1 (printed pp. 199-200): FE_r = Q_r/Q_total; Q_i = m_i n_i F / MW_i with n_i the electrons needed to form i from nitrate; total CE = sum of partial CEs of all reactions except H2 evolution (alternatively 1 - FE_H2 from on-line GC). Partial CEs exclude products not analysed, e.g. nitramide.
conditions.N2O: N2O was detected in all experiments (about 5 % selectivity at -2.8 V, printed p. 87) but has no column; the total excludes it

checks.row_sequences_dash_note: The page prints the minus sign of each potential as an en dash (U+2013); the sequences above are written with an ASCII hyphen, so 'found_on_page: true' holds after dash normalisation. Independent re-check 2026-10-20 (data/digitized_inputs/thesis_tables_verification.json): 0 of 5 found exactly, 5 of 5 after normalisation.
checks.text_printed_p88: CEs of all products and the total decrease with increasingly negative potential (hydrogen evolution favoured): holds for every column

transcription_method: thesis text layer: per-page text layer of the National Archive of PhD Theses online reader (EKT freader), read and typed in by an agent on 2026-10-20; table layout reconstructed by hand from the flattened text; every row's printed number sequence was checked by script to occur verbatim on the cited page (for this table after normalising the page's en dashes to '-'; see checks.row_sequences_dash_note) (literature/extraction_scripts/thesis_tables/build_tables.py). Page images of these pages were not viewed. Not yet re-checked by a person.
